e: Partial calque of German Erlkönig (literally “alder-king”), a mistranslation of Danish ellerkonge (“king of the elves”).
q: This line, and indeed the whole passage (lines 653-664), allude to the well-known poem by Goethe about the erlking, hoary enchanter of the elf-haunted alderwood, who falls in love with the delicate little boy of a belated traveler.

Named for Jozef Erlichman, electron microprobe analyst at the NASA Ames Research Center.
Erlichman + -ite
Named after Danish mathematician and engineer Agner Krarup Erlang (1878–1929).
q: One erlang (1 Erl) is defined as the amount of traffic generated by the user when he or she uses one traffic channel for one hour (this one hour is usually the busy hour of the network).
